an American-born Bulgarian former professional [[basketball]] player. He was born in the United States, but also holds Bulgarian citizenship, and has played for the senior men's [[Bulgarian national basketball team]].[https://www.eurobasket.com/Bulgaria/basketball.aspx?NewsID=280745 Cedric Simmons in Bulgaria on his first minutes for the NT and PAO rumors.] A {{convert|6|ft|9|in|cm|adj=mid|-tall}} [[power forward]]-[[Center (basketball)|center]], Simmons was selected by the [[New Orleans Hornets]], in the first round (15th overall pick over all) of the [[2006 NBA draft]]. ==College career== Simmons played [[college basketball]] for the [[NC State Wolfpack men's basketball|NC State Wolfpack]]. As a sophomore, he averaged 11.8 points, 6.3 rebounds, 1.7 assists, and 2.5 blocks per game. ==Professional career== Simmons was selected with the 15th pick in the [[2006 NBA draft]] by the [[New Orleans Hornets]]. On July 5, 2006, he signed with the Hornets.[https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/2510388 Hornets officially sign draft picks, waive Norris] On September 29, 2007, he was traded to the [[Cleveland Cavaliers]], in exchange for guard [[David Wesley]].{{cite web|title=Cavaliers Acquire Cedric Simmons |url=http://www.nba.com/cavaliers/news/cedric_simmons_signed_070929.html |work=NBA.com |date=2007-09-29 |accessdate=2009-04-09 |url-status=dead |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20071011041150/http://www.nba.com/cavaliers/news/cedric_simmons_signed_070929.html |archivedate=October 11, 2007 }} On January 2, 2008, he was assigned to the [[Rio Grande Valley Vipers]] of the [[NBA D-League]].{{Cite web |url=http://www.nba.com/dleague/riograndevalley/simmons_080102.html |title=Cleveland Cavaliers Assign Cedric Simmons To Rio Grande Valley |website=[[NBA.com]] |access-date=2016-02-17 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20091217232810/http://www.nba.com/dleague/riograndevalley/simmons_080102.html |archive-date=2009-12-17 |url-status=dead }} He was recalled by Cleveland on January 11, 2008.{{Cite web |url=http://www.nba.com/dleague/riograndevalley/simmons_080111.html |title=Cavaliers Recall Cedric Simmons From Rio Grande Valley Vipers |website=[[NBA.com]] |access-date=2016-02-17 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20091217232827/http://www.nba.com/dleague/riograndevalley/simmons_080111.html |archive-date=2009-12-17 |url-status=dead }} On February 21, 2008, he was traded to the [[Chicago Bulls]], in a three-team trade, along with [[Drew Gooden (basketball)|Drew Gooden]], [[Larry Hughes]], and [[Shannon Brown]], in exchange for [[Ben Wallace (basketball)|Ben Wallace]] and [[Joe Smith (basketball)|Joe Smith]].{{cite web|title=Bulls acquire Gooden and Hughes in three-team trade |url=http://www.nba.com/bulls/news/hughes_gooden_080221.html |work=NBA.com |date=2008-02-21 |accessdate=2009-04-09 |url-status=dead |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20080306200219/http://www.nba.com/bulls/news/hughes_gooden_080221.html |archivedate=March 6, 2008 }} On March 15, 2008, he was assigned to the [[Iowa Energy]] of the D-League.{{Cite web |url=http://www.nba.com/dleague/iowa/bulls_080315.html |title=Chicago Bulls Assign Shannon Brown and Cedric Simmons To Iowa Energy |website=[[NBA.com]] |access-date=2016-02-17 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20111102183254/http://www.nba.com/dleague/iowa/bulls_080315.html |archive-date=2011-11-02 |url-status=dead }} On April 1, 2008, he was recalled by the Bulls.[http://basketball.realgm.com/wiretap/189068/Bulls-Recall-Brown-Simmons-From-D-League Bulls Recall Brown, Simmons From D-League] On February 18, 2009, he was traded to the [[Sacramento Kings]], along with Drew Gooden and [[Andrés Nocioni]], for [[Brad Miller (basketball)|Brad Miller]] and [[John Salmons]].{{cite web |url=http://www.nba.com/kings/news/kings_press_release0209.html |title=KINGS ACQUIRE FOUR PLAYERS IN THREE-TEAM TRADE |work=NBA.com |date=2009-02-18 |accessdate=2009-02-19}} On December 4, 2009, he was signed by the [[Idaho Stampede]] of the NBA D-League.{{Cite web |url=http://www.nba.com/dleague/idaho/stampede_add_simmons_roster_2009_12_13.html |title=STAMPEDE ADD CEDRIC SIMMONS TO ROSTER |website=[[NBA.com]] |access-date=2016-02-17 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160610055826/http://www.nba.com/dleague/idaho/stampede_add_simmons_roster_2009_12_13.html |archive-date=2016-06-10 |url-status=dead }} In late January 2010, he left the Stampede and signed with the [[Dongguan Leopards]] of China for the rest of the [[2009–10 CBA season]].{{Cite web |url=http://www.wect.com/Global/story.asp?S=11891757 |title=Cedric Simmons joins Chinese team. |access-date=2010-02-02 |archive-date=2012-02-22 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120222080656/http://www.wect.com/Global/story.asp?S=11891757 |url-status=dead }} After the end of the Chinese season, on April 2, 2010, he signed with [[Union Kavala B.C.|Kavala]] of the [[Greek Basket League|Greek League]] for the rest of the season.[http://www.sportando.com/en/europe/greece/80580/kavala-signs-cedric-simmons.html Kavala signs Cedric Simmons] In August 2011, he signed with [[CB Estudiantes|Estudiantes]] of the Spanish [[Liga ACB]] for the 2011–12 season.[http://www.sportando.net/eng/europe/spain/30327/asefa_estudiantes_lands_former_nba_cedric_simmons.html Asefa Estudiantes lands former NBA Cedric Simmons.] On August 17, 2012, Simmons signed with [[New Basket Brindisi]] of the Italian [[Lega Basket Serie A|Serie A]] for the 2012–13 season.[http://www.sportando.com/en/italy/serie-a/94605/enel-brindisi-lands-cedric-simmons.html Enel Brindisi lands Cedric Simmons] On July 1, 2013, he signed a three-year deal with the Greek club [[Olympiacos B.C.|Olympiacos]].[http://www.sportando.com/en/europe/greece/102834/olympiacos-hands-simmons-three-year-deal.html Olympiacos hands Simmons three-year deal] On November 4, 2014, he parted ways with Olympiacos.[http://www.sportando.com/en/europe/greece/139962/olympiacos-cedric-simmons-part-ways.html Olympiacos, Cedric Simmons part ways] Four days later, he signed with his former team New Basket Brindisi.[http://www.sportando.com/en/italy/serie-a/140422/cedric-simmons-returns-to-enel-brindisi.html Cedric Simmons returns to Enel Brindisi] After suffering a season-ending knee injury, he was replaced in the line-up by [[Micheal Eric]] on December 13, 2014.[http://www.basketinside.com/2014/brindisi-sembra-conclusa-la-trattativa-con-il-pivot-sara-michael-eric-il-sostituto-di-cedric-simmons/ Brindisi, sembra conclusa la trattativa con il pivot, sarà Michael Eric il sostituto di Cedric Simmons] {{in lang|it}} On August 8, 2015, he signed with [[Royal Halı Gaziantep]] of the [[Turkish Basketball League]].[http://www.sportando.com/en/europe/turkey/172114/gaziante-announces-cedric-simmons.html Gaziantep announces Cedric Simmons] However, later that month he parted ways with Gaziantep before appearing in a game for them.[http://www.sportando.com/en/europe/turkey/173560/gaziantep-cedric-simmons-part-ways.html Gaziantep, Cedric Simmons part ways] On January 28, 2016, he signed a two-week contract with [[Maccabi Tel Aviv B.C.|Maccabi Tel Aviv]].[http://www.sportando.com/en/europe/israel/189300/maccabi-tel-aviv-announces-cedric-simmons.html Maccabi Tel Aviv announces Cedric Simmons] Following the expiration of his contract, he parted ways with Maccabi on February 12.[http://www.sportando.com/en/europe/israel/190807/maccabi-tel-aviv-release-cedric-simmons.html Maccabi Tel Aviv release Cedric Simmons] Two days later, he signed with [[Real Betis Baloncesto|Baloncesto Sevilla]] for the rest of the season.[http://www.sportando.com/en/europe/spain/190911/sevilla-signs-cedric-simmons.html Sevilla signs Cedric Simmons] However, after failing to pass physicals his contract with the Spanish team was voided.[http://www.sportando.com/en/europe/spain/191203/cedric-simmons-did-not-pass-physicals-with-sevilla.html Cedric Simmons did not pass physicals with Sevilla] On August 19, 2016, Simmons joined [[KK Budućnost|Budućnost VOLI]] for a tryout period.[http://www.sportando.com/en/europe/montenegro/209896/cedric-simmons-joins-kk-buducnost-voli-for-a-tryout-period.html Cedric Simmons joins KK Buducnost Voli for a tryout period] However, he did not signed a contract. On November 27, 2016, he signed with Estonian club [[BC Kalev]]/Cramo.[http://www.bckalev.ee/lahiajal-korvi-alla-joudu-juurde/ Lähiajal korvi alla jõudu juurde] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161201080307/http://www.bckalev.ee/lahiajal-korvi-alla-joudu-juurde/ |date=2016-12-01 }} {{in lang|et}} Two days later, he made his debut for Kalev/Cramo in a 102–69 win over [[Audentes/Noortekoondis|G4S Noorteliiga]], recording 6 points in 14 minutes.[http://www.eurobasket.com/boxScores/Estonia/2016/1129_8352_2763.asp Noorteliiga - Kalev/Cramo 69-102] On August 1, 2017, he re-signed with Kalev/Cramo for one more season.[http://www.sportando.com/en/europe/estonia/243135/bc-kalev-inks-bojan-subotic-re-signs-cedric-simmons.html#refresh_ce BC Kalev inks Bojan Subotic, re-signs Cedric Simmons] ==National team career== Simmons has been a member of the senior men's [[Bulgarian national basketball team]]. He played at the [[FIBA EuroBasket 2013 qualification]] tournament, where he averaged 10.4 points, 8.3 rebounds, and 1.3 blocks per game.[http://www.fibaeurope.com/cid_KNce8jInH7Qj1EsyH5rjn2.playerID_80374.compID_%7Bd166e39e-2323-4863-b229-76357a926fa2%7D.season_2013.roundID_8721.teamID_253.html FIBAEurope.com CEDRIC SIMMONS (BULGARIA).] ==Personal life== On December 12, 2007, Simmons's girlfriend, Sabrina Acevedo, gave birth to the couple's son at Hillcrest Hospital in [[Mayfield Heights, Ohio]].[https://web.archive.org/web/20071218102126/http://www.nba.com/cavaliers/news/recap_sixers_071215.html Cavaliers: Wine and Gold's Winter Woes Continue.] == NBA career statistics == {{NBA player
